A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of CFTR mutations in individuals with suspected PCD is higher than the general population, but the prevalence of CF (2 pathogenic CF mutations) is still low.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a single pathogenetic variant in CFTR is not likely to cause PCD, but 2 or more variants can cause mild CFTR disease, and these patients can be misdiagnose as PCD.
CFTR testing should be considered in individuals suspected of having PCD, especially when genetic testing results are negative or uncertain.
CF should be considered even in individuals who test negative for PCD, and CF is more common among individuals with negative genetic testing for PCD than in the general population.
